title: Constitutional Interface of Administrative Law — Rights, Review and Structure

content.overview: Administrative law interfaces with the Constitution at three points: fundamental-rights constraints on administrative action, the judicial-review jurisdiction of constitutional courts, and the structural provisions that create or limit administrative institutions (including tribunals).
content.glance: Map the administrative action to the engaged constitutional provision (Arts 14/19/21/32/226/323A); state the interface consequence (invalidity, review, structural limit).
content.study: Every significant administrative-law doctrine in India has a constitutional interface. Non-arbitrariness is Article 14; fair procedure affecting liberty is Article 21; writ remedies are Articles 32 and 226; tribunal design is Articles 323A/323B subject to basic structure. The interface means that administrative power is never purely statutory — it is always constitutionally conditioned. Current-law framing: name the constitutional provision before the administrative doctrine.

sections.heading: Rights Interface
sections.body: Articles 14, 19 and 21 constrain the substance and procedure of administrative action.

sections.heading: Review Interface
sections.body: Articles 32, 136, 226 and 227 supply the jurisdictional basis for judicial control.

sections.heading: Structural Interface
sections.body: Articles 323A/323B and the basic-structure doctrine condition tribunal and institutional design.

sections.heading: Consequence of Interface
sections.body: Statutory power inconsistent with the Constitution is void; review cannot be fully ousted.

examples.title: Rights interface
examples.body: A blacklisting order without hearing engages Article 14 and Article 21 interests; the interface requires fairness.

examples.title: Structural interface
examples.body: A tribunal statute excludes High Court review. The structural interface (basic structure) renders the ouster ineffective.

hypotheticals.question: Can a statute validly exclude all constitutional review of administrative action?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Judicial review under Articles 226/227 is part of the basic structure.

hypotheticals.question: Does every administrative decision engage Article 21?
hypotheticals.analysis: Only where life or personal liberty is affected; not every administrative inconvenience rises to Article 21.

misconceptions.trap: Administrative law operates outside the Constitution.
misconceptions.correction: It is constitutionally conditioned at every significant point.

misconceptions.trap: Statutory finality clauses defeat constitutional review.
misconceptions.correction: Constitutional judicial review cannot be ousted by ordinary legislation.

cases.name: L. Chandra Kumar v Union of India
cases.issue: Whether High Court review can be excluded.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Articles 226/227 review is part of the basic structure.

cases.name: Maneka Gandhi v Union of India
cases.ratioDecidendi: Procedure must be fair, just and reasonable.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a constitutional-interface problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the administrative action. II. Map the engaged constitutional provision. III. State the interface consequence. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Action identified; constitutional provision; interface doctrine; precise relief.

examTips: Name the article before the doctrine.
content.migrationNote: Substantive enhancement. Case-law verification remains a separate gate.

learningObjectives: Map administrative action to constitutional provisions.
Distinguish rights, review and structural interfaces.
State the consequence of constitutional inconsistency.
enhancement.definition: The constitutional interface is the set of points at which administrative power is conditioned by fundamental rights, judicial review and structural limits.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Administrative power is always constitutionally conditioned; statutory finality cannot oust constitutional review.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Rights, review and structure form the three principal interfaces.
